correctness.rationale: PASS applies to the complete corrected /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md. In the frozen proof, line 22 allows b=t when t is nonzero and a≠t in characteristic two; this gives c=a, contrary to the asserted pairwise distinctness (e.g. t=1, b=1, a independent of 1 over F2 in F8). The repaired proof also excludes t, leaving at most four forbidden choices for q≥8; it verifies each distinctness constraint. The Finding and hypotheses are unchanged. I checked the other branches: coprimality with the unit group order makes every unit a d-th power; any nonunit base has d-th power zero at m≤d. The odd-field argument avoids all five bad choices, and three distinct nonzero residues lift by solving for the third unit. At q=5 the field omits zero, but the residue pattern (1,1,3) covers that fiber at m≥2; at q=4 the field covers only zero, while (a,a,t) with a≠t and distinct lifts supplies the nonzero fibers. At q=3,m=2 the only candidates for zero are three units from one residue class (no nonzero nonunit powers); these total 3 or 6 modulo nine. This necessity step is clarified in the repair. At m≥3 the same-residue construction avoids 0,z,z/2 in an ideal of size at least 9; the other target residues use two distinct lifts of the repeated residue. At q=2 parity forbids even targets at m≤d. At m>d the nonzero even value 2^d and two distinct odd values cover every even target, with choices 1 and 3 for the first odd value never both colliding. The three-odd construction covers all odd targets, including the two exceptional residues 5 and 7 where the indicated replacements are distinct modulo 2^m≥16. In F5 the pair sums cover all five residues, unlike the triple sums. Inspected the frozen checker without executing it; separate bounded checks validated the repaired XOR construction for every allowed t,a,b in F8, the mod 9 and mod 27 thresholds at d=5, and the m=d versus m=d+1 binary thresholds at d=3,5,7. These corroborate only finite cases; the repaired proof supplies the universal statements.
